# Fun language, full AI context

Ontology v0.1.0 for Fun 9.5.7. Every example below is executed by `fun ontology/tools/build.fun --check`.

## Syntax

### Hello world (`syntax.hello`)

A Fun script is a sequence of statements; `?.` prints a value and a newline.

Transfer: js `console.log('Hello')`; py `print('Hello')`; c `puts("Hello");`;

```fun
?. 'Hello, Fun!';
```
Expected output:
```text
Hello, Fun!
```

### Statements and semicolons (`syntax.statement`)

Statements end with `;`. Block closers (`end if`, `end fun`, `end class`, `end do`, `end loop`, `end try`) may omit the following `;`. Newlines are not statement boundaries.

Transfer: js `statement;`; py `one statement per line (Fun does not use indentation)`;

```fun
var a = 1;
var b = a
  + 2;
?. b;
```
Expected output:
```text
3
```

### Comments (`syntax.comment`)

Both `#` and `//` start a line comment. `#* ... *#` is a block comment.

Transfer: js `// comment`; py `# comment`;

```fun
# a hash comment
// a slash comment
#* a block
   comment *#
?. 1;
```
Expected output:
```text
1
```

### Variables (`syntax.var`)

Declare with `var name = expr;` or `var name;` (nil). There is no `let` or `const`; identifiers are case-insensitive.

Transfer: js `let x = 1; const y = 2;`; py `x = 1`; c `int x = 1;`;

```fun
var x = 1;
var y;
?. x;
?. y = nil;
```
Expected output:
```text
1
True
```

### Assignment and equality (`syntax.assignment`)

A statement `x = expr;` assigns; the same `=` inside an expression compares. `<>` and `!=` both mean not-equal. Compound assignment uses `+= -= *= &=`.

Transfer: js `x = 1; if (a === b)`; py `x = 1; if a == b:`; c `x = 1; if (a == b)`;

```fun
var x = 1;
x = x + 2;
?. x;
?. x = 3;
?. x <> 4;
```
Expected output:
```text
3
True
True
```

### Print and output (`syntax.print`)

The `?.` operator prints with a newline, `?,` prints with a space, and `?:` prints with a tab. All three accept any value.

Transfer: js `console.log(value)`; py `print(value)`; c `printf("%v\n", value);`;

```fun
?, 'a';
?: 'b';
?. 'c';
```
Expected output:
```text
a b	c
```

### Named functions (`syntax.function`)

A `fun name(params) ... end fun;` returns the value assigned to `result`; `return expr;` exits early. `result` is not reset on entry, so initialize it explicitly.

Transfer: js `function f(a, b) { return a + b; }`; py `def f(a, b): return a + b`; c `int f(int a, int b) { return a + b; }`;

```fun
fun add(a, b)
  result = a + b;
end fun;
?. add(2, 3);
```
Expected output:
```text
5
```

### Lambdas (`syntax.lambda`)

A lambda `a -> expr` takes one argument; `(a, b) -> expr` takes several. A braced body is a block that must assign `result`.

Transfer: js `a => a * 2`; py `lambda a: a * 2`;

```fun
use 'lib-set.fun';
var f = a -> a * 2;
?. f(3);
var nums = [1, 2, 3];
?. (nums | map(a -> a + 1)).@toJson();
```
Expected output:
```text
6
[2,3,4]
```

### Conditionals (`syntax.if`)

The form `if c then ... elsif c2 then ... else ... end if;` uses Fun truthiness; use explicit comparisons for clarity.

Transfer: js `if (c) { } else { }`; py `if c: ... else: ...`;

```fun
var n = 2;
if n = 1 then
  ?. 'one';
elsif n = 2 then
  ?. 'two';
else
  ?. 'other';
end if;
```
Expected output:
```text
two
```

### Case (`syntax.case`)

The form `case expr is when v do ... else ... end case;` matches values.

Transfer: js `switch (x) { case 1: ... }`; py `match x: case 1: ...`;

```fun
var x = 2;
case x is
  when 1 do ?. 'one';
  when 2 do ?. 'two';
  else ?. 'other';
end case;
```
Expected output:
```text
two
```

### Loops (`syntax.loop`)

Forms: `for i = a to b do ... end do;`, `for k: v in set do ... end do;`, `while c do ... end do;`, and `loop ... exit when c; ... end loop;`. `next when c;` skips.

Transfer: js `for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {}`; py `for i in range(n):`;

```fun
var total = 0;
for i = 1 to 3 do
  total += i;
end do;
?. total;
var m = 0;
loop
  m += 1;
  exit when m >= 2;
end loop;
?. m;
```
Expected output:
```text
6
2
```

### Errors (`syntax.try`)

The form `try ... except ... finally ... end try;` catches `raise` and runtime errors. `runtime.lastError()` exposes message, file, line and stack.

Transfer: js `try { } catch (e) { }`; py `try: ... except Exception as e: ...`;

```fun
try
  raise 'boom';
except
  ?. 'caught';
end try;
```
Expected output:
```text
caught
```

### Classes (`syntax.class`)

A `class Name(params) ... end class;` body runs as the constructor; `var` fields become members, `fun` declarations become methods, `this` is the instance and `base` the parent. Inherit with `class Child = Parent()`.

Transfer: js `class C { constructor(x) { this.x = x; } }`; py `class C: def __init__(self, x): self.x = x`;

```fun
class Point(x, y)
  var x = x;
  var y = y;
  fun sum() result = x + y; end fun;
end class;
var p = Point(2, 3);
?. p.sum();
?. p.x;
```
Expected output:
```text
5
2
```

### Modules (`syntax.use`)

The statement `use 'lib-set.fun';` links a module by file name; `use 'x.fun' as ns;` namespaces it. Paths resolve relative to the script and the runtime `lib/` directory.

Transfer: js `import x from './x.js'`; py `import x`; c `#include "x.h"`;

```fun
use 'lib-set.fun';
var xs = [1, 2, 3];
?. (xs | map(a -> a * 2)).@toJson();
```
Expected output:
```text
[2,4,6]
```

### Lists and maps (`syntax.collection`)

A list literal `[1, 2, 3]` is a list. `new [k: v]` is a string-keyed map (called a set in Fun). Both support `@count`, `@has`, `@add`, and JSON conversion.

Transfer: js `[1, 2]; {a: 1}`; py `[1, 2]; {'a': 1}`; c `int a[2] = {1, 2};`;

```fun
var xs = [1, 2, 3];
var m = new [name: 'Ada'];
?. xs.@count();
?. m.name;
?. m['name'];
xs.@add(4);
?. xs.@toJson();
```
Expected output:
```text
3
Ada
Ada
[1,2,3,4]
```

### Member access (`syntax.member`)

Forms `obj.key`, `obj['key']` and `obj.['1']` read members; a missing member compares equal to nil. Postfix `?` makes a member or its base optional: `x?.k?`.

Transfer: js `obj.key; obj['key']; a?.k`; py `obj.key; obj['key']`;

```fun
var m = new [name: 'Ada'];
?. m.name;
?. m['name'];
?. m.missing = nil;
var none = nil;
?. none?.name? = nil;
```
Expected output:
```text
Ada
Ada
True
True
```

### Built-in methods (`syntax.method`)

Engine-provided methods use `@`: `x.@toJson()`, `s.@count()`, `m.@('group')`. Methods you write in a class are called without `@`.

Transfer: js `value.toString()`; py `len(value)`;

```fun
var xs = [1, 2, 3];
?. xs.@count();
?. xs.@toJson();
```
Expected output:
```text
3
[1,2,3]
```

### Pipe (`syntax.pipe`)

The pipe `value | f` passes the value as the last argument of `f`. `map(f)` takes the list last, so it composes; `filter(list, f)` takes the list first, so call it directly.

Transfer: js `xs.map(f).filter(p)`; py `filter(p, map(f, xs))`;

```fun
use 'lib-set.fun';
var xs = [1, 2, 3, 4];
var ys = xs | map(a -> a * 10);
?. ys.@toJson();
```
Expected output:
```text
[10,20,30,40]
```

### Strings (`syntax.string`)

Single, double and backtick quotes all delimit strings. There are no backslash escapes such as `\n`; use `10.toChar()` for a newline or a multiline backtick string. `$name` interpolation is done by `.eval()`.

Transfer: js `"a\nb"`; py `"a\nb"`;

```fun
var a = 'x' & 10.toChar() & 'y';
?. a.length();
var b = 'hello';
?. 'say $b'.eval();
var c = 'one' & 10.toChar() & 'two';
?. c;
```
Expected output:
```text
3
say hello
one
two
```

### Regular expressions (`syntax.regex`)

Regex literals are `/pattern/flags`, `%pattern%flags` or `$'pattern'flags`. Use `=~` / `!~` to test, `.match()` to extract, `.replace()` to rewrite.

Transfer: js `s.match(/\d+/g)`; py `re.findall(r'\d+', s)`;

```fun
var s = 'a1b22';
?. s.match(/\d+/g).@toJson();
?. s.replace(/\d+/g, (m) -> '[' & m.@(0) & ']');
?. (s =~ /^a/) <> nil;
```
Expected output:
```text
["1","22"]
a[1]b[22]
True
```

### JSON (`syntax.json`)

The built-in `value.@toJson()` emits JSON; `value.@toJson(json: true)` quotes keys. Parse with `text.getJson(json: true)`. `text.getJson(fd: true)` parses FD.

Transfer: js `JSON.parse(s); JSON.stringify(v)`; py `json.loads(s); json.dumps(v)`;

```fun
var m = '{"a": 1, "b": [2, 3]}'.getJson(json: true);
?. m.a;
?. m.b[1];
?. m.@toJson(json: true);
```
Expected output:
```text
1
3
{"a":1,"b":[2,3]}
```

### FD data (`syntax.fd`)

FD is Fun's indentation data notation: `key value` lines, `- item` lists, no braces. `text.getJson(fd: true)` parses it and `value.@toJson(fd: true)` emits it.

Transfer: js `YAML-like nested objects`; py `dict / list`;

```fun
var s = 'name Ada' & 10.toChar() & 'tags' & 10.toChar() & '  - math' & 10.toChar() & '  - code';
var m = s.getJson(fd: true);
?. m.name;
?. m.tags.@count();
```
Expected output:
```text
Ada
2
```

### Operator overloading (`syntax.operator`)

An operator is a field keyed by its symbol. In `this['#'] = you -> ...`, `me` is the receiver and `you` the right operand.

Transfer: js `Symbol.toPrimitive`; py `__add__`;

```fun
class Num(me)
  this['#'] = you -> (me + you) * me * you;
end class;
var n = Num(2);
?. n .# 3;
```
Expected output:
```text
30
```

## Semantics

### Missing values compare to nil (`sem.missing-is-nil`)

Reading a missing member, key or index yields a value that compares equal to nil. This makes `if x = nil then x = init; end if` safe.

Transfer: js `undefined == null`; py `None`;

```fun
var m = new [];
?. m.nope = nil;
?. m['nope'] = nil;
?. m[0] = nil;
```
Expected output:
```text
True
True
True
```

### nil acts as zero in arithmetic (`sem.nil-arithmetic`)

A nil operand in `+ - * / div mod` is treated as 0, and as '' for strings. `x += 1` therefore works on a fresh key. The flip side is that a missing value also compares equal to 0.

Transfer: js `undefined + 1 -> NaN`; py `None + 1 -> TypeError`;

```fun
var m = new [];
m.k += 1;
?. m.k;
var z;
?. z + 1;
?. m.@has('k');
?. m.@has('no');
```
Expected output:
```text
1
1
True
False
```

### or/and return values (`sem.or-value`)

Operators `or` and `and` return one of their operands, Lua style: `nil or 5` is 5, `7 or 5` is 7. This powers default values.

Transfer: js `x ?? default`; py `x if x is not None else default`;

```fun
?. (nil or 5);
?. (7 or 5);
?. (nil and 5) = nil;
```
Expected output:
```text
5
7
True
```

### result is not reset (`sem.result`)

Each function has one `result` slot. It is not cleared on entry, so a call at the same stack depth can see the previous value. Always initialize `result`.

Transfer: js `return undefined by default`; py `return None by default`;

```fun
fun f(n)
  if n > 0 then result = n; end if;
end fun;
?. f(1);
?. f(0);
fun g(n)
  result = 0;
  if n > 0 then result = n; end if;
end fun;
?. g(1);
?. g(0);
```
Expected output:
```text
1
1
1
0
```

### Identifiers are case-insensitive (`sem.case-insensitive`)

Variables, functions, members and built-in method names all fold case. Avoid local names that differ from another symbol only by case.

Transfer: js `case-sensitive`; py `case-sensitive`;

```fun
var Foo = 1;
?. foo;
var m = new [name: 'Ada'];
?. m.NAME;
?. 'Hi'.UPPER();
```
Expected output:
```text
1
Ada
HI
```

### Named arguments (`sem.named-args`)

Call sites may name arguments: `f(b: 2, a: 1)`. Missing arguments are nil, so defaults are written as `if p = nil then p = default; end if`.

Transfer: js `f({a: 1, b: 2})`; py `f(a=1, b=2)`;

```fun
fun greet(name, punct)
  if punct = nil then punct = '!'; end if;
  result = 'Hi ' & name & punct;
end fun;
?. greet('Ada');
?. greet(punct: '?', name: 'Bob');
```
Expected output:
```text
Hi Ada!
Hi Bob?
```

### Value types (`sem.type`)

The method `.type()` returns 0 nil, 3 int, 5 real, 6 currency, 7 time, 8 string, 11 bool, -1 other. Integers are 32-bit unless explicitly 64-bit.

Transfer: js `typeof x`; py `type(x)`;

```fun
var n = 1;
var s = 'x';
var z;
var b = true;
?. n.type();
?. s.type();
?. z.type();
?. b.type();
```
Expected output:
```text
3
8
0
11
```

### Maps and lists are references (`sem.reference`)

Assigning a map or list copies the reference. Mutating one alias is visible through the other; use `@clone()` for an independent copy.

Transfer: js `objects are references`; py `lists/dicts are references`;

```fun
use 'lib-set.fun';
var a = [x: 1];
var b = a;
b.x = 2;
?. a.x;
var c = a.@clone();
c.x = 3;
?. a.x;
?. c.x;
```
Expected output:
```text
2
2
3
```

### User methods vs built-in methods (`sem.user-vs-builtin`)

Methods declared with `fun` inside a class are called as `obj.method()`. Engine methods are called as `obj.@method()`. The `@` is the dispatch marker, not part of the name.

```fun
class Box(v)
  var v = v;
  fun get() result = v; end fun;
end class;
var b = Box(7);
?. b.get();
```
Expected output:
```text
7
```

## Built-ins

### @toJson (`builtin.tojson`)

The built-in serializer. Default output is JSON-like with bare keys; `json: true` quotes keys, and `fd: true` emits FD.

Transfer: js `JSON.stringify(value)`; py `json.dumps(value)`;

```fun
var m = new [a: 1, b: [2]];
?. m.@toJson(json: true);
```
Expected output:
```text
{"a":1,"b":[2]}
```

## Modules

### lib-set (`module.lib-set`)

Collection helpers in pure Fun: `map`, `filter`, `find`, `sort`, `compose`, `range`, `@clone`, and more.

Transfer: js `Array.prototype.map/filter`; py `map/filter`;

```fun
use 'lib-set.fun';
?. ([1, 2, 3] | map(a -> a * 2)).@toJson();
```
Expected output:
```text
[2,4,6]
```

### lib-json (`module.lib-json`)

JSON and FD parse/stringify helpers. The underlying built-ins are `.getJson()` and `.@toJson()`, documented in `lib-json.fun`.

```fun
var m = '{"a": 1}'.getJson(json: true);
?. m.@toJson(json: true);
```
Expected output:
```text
{"a":1}
```

### runtime (`module.runtime`)

The calls `runtime.source()`, `runtime.stack()`, `runtime.lastError()` expose source locations, call stacks and the last caught error.

Transfer: js `new Error().stack`; py `traceback`;

```fun
use 'runtime.fun';
try
  raise 'boom';
except
  var e = runtime.lastError();
  ?. e.message = 'boom';
end try;
```
Expected output:
```text
True
```

### fs (`module.fs`)

Portable filesystem helpers: `mkdirAll`, `list`, `walk`, `removeAll`, `tempFile`, `tempDir`, `atomicWrite` and byte streams.

```fun
use 'fs.fun';
var d = fs.tempDir('fun-ontology-');
?. d <> '';
fs.removeAll(d);
```
Expected output:
```text
True
```

### cli (`module.cli`)

A command-line framework: subcommands, flags, aliases, env fallback, required flags, hooks and help.

```fun
?. 'See fun/lib/cli.fun';
```
Expected output:
```text
See fun/lib/cli.fun
```

### http-server (`module.http-server`)

An HTTP server with routing, path parameters, middleware, static files and a blocking poll loop. Handlers are `fun(req, res)`.

```fun
?. 'See fun/lib/http-server.fun';
```
Expected output:
```text
See fun/lib/http-server.fun
```

### http-client (`module.http-client`)

An HTTP client with helpers for JSON, headers, timeouts and TLS. `use 'http-client.fun';`.

Transfer: js `fetch(url)`; py `requests.get(url)`;

```fun
?. 'See fun/lib/http-client.fun';
```
Expected output:
```text
See fun/lib/http-client.fun
```

### lib-fd (`module.lib-fd`)

FD parse and emit helpers. The underlying built-ins are `text.getJson(fd: true)` and `value.@toJson(fd: true)`.

```fun
var m = 'a 1'.getJson(fd: true);
?. m.a;
```
Expected output:
```text
1
```

### lib-type (`module.lib-type`)

Type conversion helpers: `toStr`, `toNum`, `toTime`, `toByte`, `toChar`, `fromByte`, `eq` and `type`.

```fun
var n = 1;
?. n.type();
```
Expected output:
```text
3
```

### lib-host (`module.lib-host`)

Host detection and libc binding: `LibC()`, `IsWindows()`, `HostCurrPath()`, and the `'host'.arg()` facts.

```fun
use 'lib-host.fun';
var getpid = LibC().getapi('getpid', ':i');
?. getpid() > 0;
```
Expected output:
```text
True
```

### lib-cwinapi (`module.lib-cwinapi`)

Windows helper: `CWin32API('user32.dll', 'int MessageBoxA(HWND, LPCSTR, LPCSTR, UINT);')` parses a C prototype and exposes named arguments.

```fun
?. 'Windows only: use CWin32API(dll, prototype)';
```
Expected output:
```text
Windows only: use CWin32API(dll, prototype)
```

### lib-cstruct (`module.lib-cstruct`)

The call `CStruct('struct Point { int x; int y; };', [x: 3, y: 4])` computes offsets and padding and exposes a pointer-addressable buffer.

```fun
?. 'Use CStruct(declaration, values) for C layouts';
```
Expected output:
```text
Use CStruct(declaration, values) for C layouts
```

## Idioms

### Default value (`idiom.default`)

Use `or` to supply a default for nil or false. `x = x or default;`.

Transfer: js `name = name || 'anonymous'`; py `name = name or 'anonymous'`;

```fun
fun greet(name)
  name = name or 'anonymous';
  result = 'Hi ' & name;
end fun;
?. greet(nil);
?. greet('Ada');
```
Expected output:
```text
Hi anonymous
Hi Ada
```

### Safe accumulator (`idiom.accumulator`)

Seed a counter explicitly when you want the intent to be obvious across builds: `m.k = (m.k or 0) + 1;`. On 9.5.7, `m.k += 1` also yields 1.

Transfer: js `m[k] = (m[k] || 0) + 1`; py `m[k] = m.get(k, 0) + 1`;

```fun
var m = new [];
m.k = (m.k or 0) + 1;
m.k = (m.k or 0) + 1;
?. m.k;
```
Expected output:
```text
2
```

### Data pipeline (`idiom.pipeline`)

The pipeline `xs | map(f)` reads left to right. Add `use 'lib-set.fun';` first. `map` takes the list last and composes; `filter` takes the list first.

Transfer: js `xs.map(f).filter(p)`; py `[...]`;

```fun
use 'lib-set.fun';
var xs = [1, 2, 3, 4];
?. (xs | map(a -> a * a)).@toJson();
?. filter(xs, a -> a > 2).@toJson();
```
Expected output:
```text
[1,4,9,16]
[3,4]
```

### Closure counter (`idiom.closure`)

A function value captures its defining scope. Capture an argument to build a specialized function without a class.

Transfer: js `let n = 0; return () => ++n`; py `def counter(): n = 0; ...`;

```fun
fun adder(n)
  result = a -> a + n;
end fun;
var add2 = adder(2);
?. add2(3);
?. add2(10);
```
Expected output:
```text
5
12
```

### JSON round trip (`idiom.json-roundtrip`)

Parse with `.getJson(json: true)`, inspect with member access, emit with `.@toJson(json: true)`.

Transfer: js `JSON.parse / JSON.stringify`; py `json.loads / json.dumps`;

```fun
var s = '{"users": [{"name": "Ada"}]}';
var m = s.getJson(json: true);
?. m.users[0].name;
m.users[0].active = true;
?. m.@toJson(json: true);
```
Expected output:
```text
Ada
{"users":[{"name":"Ada","active":true}]}
```

### Read and write files (`idiom.file-io`)

The built-in `'path'.load()` reads a whole file; `'path'.save(text)` writes one. For directories, atomic writes and walking use `use 'fs.fun';`.

Transfer: js `fs.readFileSync(p, 'utf8')`; py `open(p).read()`;

```fun
use 'fs.fun';
var p = fs.tempFile('fun-ontology-');
p.save('hello');
?. p.load();
fs.removeAll(p);
```
Expected output:
```text
hello
```

### Command-line arguments (`idiom.cli`)

The expression `i.arg()` reads argv by position; `Argv()` (from `lib-cmdline`) returns the list. `use 'cli.fun';` gives flags, subcommands and help.

Transfer: js `process.argv`; py `sys.argv`;

```fun
?. 0.arg().length() > 0;
```
Expected output:
```text
True
```

### Call native code (`idiom.ffi`)

The call `LibC().getapi(name, signature)` or `'libname'.getapi(...)` binds a native function. The signature is `argtypes:rettype`, e.g. `':i'` for no args returning int.

Transfer: c `#include <unistd.h>; getpid();`; js `native addon`;

```fun
use 'lib-host.fun';
var getpid = LibC().getapi('getpid', ':i');
?. getpid() > 0;
```
Expected output:
```text
True
```

## Pitfalls

### There is no == (`pit.double-equals`)

Use `=` for equality inside an expression, and `<>` or `!=` for inequality. `==` is not Fun.

Transfer: js `===`; py `==`; c `==`;

```fun
?. (1 = 1);
?. (1 <> 2);
```
Expected output:
```text
True
True
```

### Newlines do not end statements (`pit.newline-is-not-a-statement`)

A newline is whitespace. Put `;` between statements; a continuation line can silently join the previous expression.

Transfer: js `automatic semicolon insertion`; py `indentation ends statements`;

```fun
var a = 1
  + 2;
?. a;
```
Expected output:
```text
3
```

### No backslash escapes (`pit.backslash-escape`)

The literal `'\n'` is a backslash followed by `n`, not a newline. Use `10.toChar()` or a multiline backtick string.

Transfer: js `"a\nb"`; py `"a\nb"`;

```fun
?. 'a\nb'.length();
?. ('a' & 10.toChar() & 'b').length();
```
Expected output:
```text
4
3
```

### Optional chaining is limited (`pit.optional-chain`)

The form `x?.k?` makes the base and the member optional. It does not make a following call optional, and `f()?.x` is not the JS form; assign to a variable first.

Transfer: js `a?.k?.()`;

```fun
fun pick(o, k) result = o?.k?; end fun;
?. pick(new [k: 7], 'k');
?. pick(nil, 'k') = nil;
```
Expected output:
```text
7
True
```

### Regex match group access (`pit.match-group`)

In a match object, `m.@(0)` is the whole match and `m.@('name')` a named group; `m.@@()` is also the whole match. `m.@()` with no argument is not valid.

Transfer: js `m[0]`; py `m.group(0)`;

```fun
var m = 'a12'.match(/(\d+)/);
?. m.@(0);
?. m.@(1);
```
Expected output:
```text
12
12
```

### A missing value also equals zero (`pit.missing-key-accumulate`)

A missing value compares equal to nil and to 0, so `if x = 0` cannot tell "absent" from "zero". Use `.@has(key)` when presence matters.

Transfer: js `Object.hasOwn(m, k)`; py `k in m`;

```fun
var m = new [];
?. m.k = nil;
?. m.k = 0;
?. m.@has('k');
m.k = 0;
?. m.@has('k');
```
Expected output:
```text
True
True
False
True
```

### [] is a list, new [] is a map (`pit.array-vs-map`)

A list literal `[1, 2]` is ordered; `new [a: 1]` is a string-keyed map. Do not use `{}` for either.

Transfer: js `[] / {}`; py `[] / {}`;

```fun
var xs = [10, 20];
var m = new [a: 10];
?. xs[1];
?. m.a;
```
Expected output:
```text
20
10
```

### result vs return (`pit.return-keyword`)

Inside `fun`, assigning `result` sets the return value; `return expr;` returns immediately. A bare `return;` returns the current `result`, which may be stale.

Transfer: js `return x`; py `return x`;

```fun
fun f()
  result = 1;
  return 2;
  result = 3;
end fun;
?. f();
```
Expected output:
```text
2
```

## Tooling

### The fun command (`tool.funcmd`)

The command `fun file.fun` runs a script; `fun test` runs a package's tests; `fun pack` builds one executable; `fun package init` creates a manifest.

Transfer: js `node hello.js`; py `python hello.py`;

```fun
?. 'Use: fun hello.fun';
```
Expected output:
```text
Use: fun hello.fun
```

### Tests (`tool.test`)

Test files are `*_test.fun`; import `test.fun` and call `test('name', { assert.equal(a, b); });`. `fun test` runs each file in a child process.

Transfer: js `test('name', () => expect(a).toBe(b))`; py `def test_name(): assert a == b`;

```fun
?. 'Write this in a *_test.fun file, then run: fun test';
```
Expected output:
```text
Write this in a *_test.fun file, then run: fun test
```

### Packages (`tool.package`)

A project has a `package.fun` manifest. `fun package init/tidy/add/remove` creates and maintains it; `fun run` runs the manifest bin.

Transfer: js `package.json / npm`; py `pyproject.toml / pip`;

```fun
?. 'fun package init myapp';
```
Expected output:
```text
fun package init myapp
```

### fun-safe (`tool.fun-safe`)

A restricted build with native code, arbitrary memory access, and file/compile access removed. Use it for plugins and untrusted scripts.

```fun
?. 'fun-safe script.fun';
```
Expected output:
```text
fun-safe script.fun
```

### fun-mt and workers (`tool.mt`)

The `fun-mt` build is the opt-in multi-threaded build. A worker parses its own module and heap; results cross as strings, with `Shared` and `Channel` for named stores.

```fun
?. 'Requires fun-mt and use lib-worker.fun';
```
Expected output:
```text
Requires fun-mt and use lib-worker.fun
```

## Platforms

### Platforms (`platform.matrix`)

Windows 95 through Windows 11, Linux x64/arm64 (glibc 2.17+), macOS x64/arm64, and nightly LoongArch64/riscv64 builds. About 0.3 MB, zero external dependencies.

```fun
var h = 'host'.arg().getJson(fd: true);
?. h.os <> '';
```
Expected output:
```text
True
```

## Tasks

### Transform JSON (`task.json-transform`)

Parse a JSON document, update a nested value, and emit JSON again.

```fun
var doc = '{"items": [{"n": 1}, {"n": 2}]}'.getJson(json: true);
for i = 0 to doc.items.@count() - 1 do
  doc.items[i].n *= 10;
end do;
?. doc.@toJson(json: true);
```
Expected output:
```text
{"items":[{"n":10},{"n":20}]}
```

### A tiny HTTP JSON endpoint (`task.hello-server`)

Create `HttpServer(port)`, register a handler that writes JSON, and call `run()`. Requires a listening socket; not executed by the ontology checker.


### Call a C function (`task.ffi-libc`)

Bind a libc function by name and signature, then call it from Fun. Use CStruct/CWin32API when a struct or a Windows prototype is involved.

```fun
use 'lib-host.fun';
var getpid = LibC().getapi('getpid', ':i');
?. getpid() > 0;
```
Expected output:
```text
True
```

### Parse argv (`task.cli-args`)

Read positional arguments with `i.arg()`, or use `Argv()`/`cli.fun` for flags and subcommands.

```fun
?. 0.arg().length() > 0;
```
Expected output:
```text
True
```
